evidence.positive: Against the running c52e8fb43 build (Mayo tenant mayo-mayo, the only tenant carrying these medications) staged patient A (pmrn or3176-fake-2508cdde..., case 75788) via the admin API, inserted a 6h-old m-aprepitant bolus (medication_orders + medication_administrations rows), evicted the Redis ContextPatient key, and POSTed /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/75788 {medicationIdentifier:m-aprepitant}. Response had needsAction=true and a w-antiemetic-early-redose result whose prompt.promptText.displayText was exactly "Patient received Aprepitant at 03:09 on 11/25/2026. Aprepitant is dosed once every 24 hours." (America/Chicago rendering of the 09:09Z dose) with citation r-antiemetic-early-redose (Gan et al., Anesth Analg, 2026) and no accept/reject text. Log: "Rule evaluated: w-antiemetic-early-redose -> true". Repeated on the same patient: granisetron tablet 10h ago then selecting m-granisetron fired naming the tablet time (23:09 on 11/24/2026); adding m-granisetron IV 3h ago then selecting m-granisetron-tablet fired naming the IV dose (06:09 on 11/25/2026), proving most-recent-dose naming across forms; palonosetron 20h ago then selecting m-palonosetron fired (13:09 on 11/24/2026).
evidence.negative: Patient B (case 76868): m-aprepitant bolus 25h ago, selecting m-aprepitant returned needsAction=false, no rule result, log "-> false APREPITANT not administered in the last 24 hours"; m-granisetron-transdermal bolus 1h ago, selecting m-granisetron and m-granisetron-tablet both stayed silent ("GRANISETRON not administered in the last 24 hours"), so a patch prior does not count. Patient C (case 82815): m-granisetron IV 1h ago, selecting m-granisetron-transdermal abstained with "m-granisetron-transdermal is a transdermal form"; selecting m-palonosetron abstained (different once-daily drug); selecting m-ondansetron-iv abstained with "is not a once-daily antiemetic"; an m-aprepitant bolus with NULL administration_date then selecting m-aprepitant abstained with no exception in the log. Control on patient C: selecting m-granisetron with the 1h IV dose fired, proving the silences above were not a staging failure. On patient A, selecting m-palonosetron while aprepitant and granisetron doses were in-window stayed silent (other drugs do not count).
evidence.red_check: Data flip on patient B: UPDATE medication_administrations SET administration_date = now() - 6h on the 25h aprepitant dose (id e1821a57...), evicted the cache, selected m-aprepitant -> needsAction=true with the warning prompt and the log line "01a21341-d6d0-7eb6-bf3e-947a2ae27bbd com.guided.orci.engine.RuleEngine : Rule evaluated: w-antiemetic-early-redose -> true" (that operation UUID, which appears only this once with -> true). Reverted to now() - 25h, evicted, reselected -> silent again ("APREPITANT not administered in the last 24 hours"). Pre-fix class swap: backed up AntiemeticEarlyRedoseWarningRule.class from /app/classes (md5 1ee182ed681d76c4c31f7f1df382d946), deleted it, docker-restarted the app; selecting m-aprepitant on patient A (6h-old aprepitant dose) returned needsAction=false and no Rule evaluated line for the rule, i.e. the positive assertion went red. Restored the class by docker cp, md5 matched 1ee182ed681d76c4c31f7f1df382d946, restarted, reselected -> warning returned with the same prompt text. A second data flip (deleting the TRANSDERMAL row from medications_medication_categories for the patch) did NOT turn red: the JVM caches medication categories, so the DB change was invisible; the row was restored (count verified 1) and that flip abandoned.

caveats: The ticket description asks for COMPLIANCE_MEDICATION_NOT_ADMINISTERED wiring and a compliance acceptance criterion; the merged spec (which the ticket says wins) states nothing is tracked for compliance, and the shipped rule has no categories or compliance details. Those ticket ACs are superseded, not met as written.

Prior doses were staged by direct SQL insert plus Redis ContextPatient eviction, not by HL7 RAS or the admin bolus endpoint; the rule reads the same patient medication-order aggregate and qa-suite ARD-007 proves the admin bolus endpoint feeds it, but the HL7-ingested path was not exercised here.

Selections were made API-only as the admin user; the dosing-form banner was not rendered in a browser (Mayo app-launch needs Epic locally). The prompt text and citation were asserted on the selection response the form consumes.

The transdermal exclusion could only be flipped by the class removal, not by data: stripping the TRANSDERMAL category in the DB was masked by the in-JVM medication cache, so the patch-tag path is covered by the shipped tag plus the unit and medication-list tests.

The rendered citation still reads "Aprepitant and palonosetron half-life: ~40 hours", which the PR review flagged as wrong for aprepitant and which was then restored as approved text; clinical content was not validated here.
Only the Mayo medication list carries aprepitant, granisetron and palonosetron; the rule is inert on demo and MGB.

automation.assessment: AntiemeticEarlyRedoseWarningRuleTest (shipped with #4833, 18 cases) covers every Fires/Abstains bullet: each drug, IV-after-tablet and the reverse, most-recent naming, the 24h boundary on both sides, patch selected and patch as prior, other drug, untimed dose, infusion-recorded dose, uncategorized medications, and the citation. MasterMedicationListTransdermalAntiemeticTest guards the Mayo patch TRANSDERMAL tag. Nothing exercises the imported Mayo list + real patient aggregate + /api/cds/medication-selection end to end; that is the one path worth locking in, and antibiotic-redose.spec.ts ARD-007/008 already establish the API-only Mayo pattern (createPatient/createOperation/addMedicationAdministration with X-Tenant-Id mayo-mayo, then the selection endpoint). Ids AER-001 and AER-002 were reserved via test-id.sh.

proposed_tests.test: AER-001 (@supplemental): on a mayo-mayo case with an m-aprepitant admin bolus 6h ago, POST /api/cds/medication-selection for m-aprepitant returns a w-antiemetic-early-redose result whose displayText matches /^Patient received Aprepitant at .* Aprepitant is dosed once every 24 hours\.$/ and cites r-antiemetic-early-redose; a second patient with the dose 25h ago returns no such result, the 6h patient being the control that proves the absence is window-driven.

AER-002 (@supplemental): on a mayo-mayo case with an m-granisetron-transdermal bolus 1h ago, selecting m-granisetron and selecting m-granisetron-transdermal both return no w-antiemetic-early-redose result; then an m-granisetron-tablet bolus 2h ago is added and selecting m-granisetron fires naming Granisetron, the control proving the earlier silence was the transdermal exclusion and not a staging failure.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Selecting aprepitant, palonosetron, or either granisetron form on a Mayo case with a dose of the same drug inside 24 hours returned the warning with the exact prompt wording, the most recent dose named, and the citation.
Negative: A dose 25 hours old, a different once-daily antiemetic, ondansetron, a granisetron patch on either side, and a dose with no time all left the selection silent.
Red check: Moving the 25-hour dose to 6 hours made the same selection fire, and removing the rule class from the running build made the positive case go silent; both were reverted and re-confirmed.

Automation: Unit coverage shipped with the PR is complete; two API-only Mayo qa-suite tests (AER-001, AER-002) are proposed to lock in the end-to-end path.
